findings.title: Detached window.setTimeout/clearTimeout breaks the debounced save in every real browser (Illegal invocation)
findings.detail: Production auto-init runs initBrowser() with env=window (script tag is deferred, so the else-branch fires), and createDebounced receives { set: env.setTimeout, clear: env.clearTimeout } — detached references invoked with this={set,clear}. Verified EMPIRICALLY in Chromium (agent-browser): t.set(fn,0) throws 'TypeError: Illegal invocation' and the timer never schedules. Every rt:form-step-changed listener call therefore throws; the debounced save — requirement 1's core mechanism and the frozen AC's 'applicant changes section -> debounced upsert persists' — never fires in production. Only the pagehide beacon (no timers) persists drafts. Node tests can't catch it: Node's setTimeout is not brand-checked and the wiring test injects fake timers.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind or wrap at the call site: createDebounced(saveNow, DEBOUNCE_MS, { set: function(fn,ms){ return env.setTimeout(fn,ms); }, clear: function(id){ env.clearTimeout(id); } }) — and add a wiring test that drives the debounce with real (or brand-checked) timers so the production seam is pinned.

findings.title: Fresh-session blank form wholesale-replaces a rich prior draft with empty-string values (empty-map guard never fires)
findings.detail: serializeForm emits EVERY non-skipped control, untouched ones as ''. A returning applicant who saved on day 1 without requesting a link reopens the blank form, enters only their email, then changes step (or clicks the continue button): the ~40-key payload of mostly '' passes the server's non-empty guard and ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields replaces day-1's answers. A later 'Email me a link' restores the wiped draft, not the rich one.
findings.recommended_fix: Client: send only dirty/changed fields (seed baseline on load). Server (defense in depth): merge jsonb (fields = application_draft.fields || EXCLUDED.fields) instead of wholesale replace, or reject payloads whose non-empty value count is implausibly low when a rich draft exists.

findings.title: Fan-out bound counts stamped rows, not sends — the documented 'max 3 continue emails per recipient per hour' is not enforced
findings.detail: The <3 check counts distinct (vacancy,email) rows stamped in the last hour; repeat sends re-stamp the SAME row so the count never grows. One draft sustains a send every 10 min (6/hr); two vacancies 12/hr; only a third distinct draft row trips the bound — up to ~4-6x the advertised ceiling in steady state.
findings.recommended_fix: Count actual sends (per-recipient send log or counter) or rewrite the comment to state the real invariant (per-draft 10-min cooldown + max 3 distinct vacancy rows stamped/hour).

findings.title: 500/vacancy draft cap counts stripped (submitted) and tombstoned (erased) rows that persist until vacancy close
findings.detail: The cap subquery has no submitted_at/erased_at filter while strip-on-submit and erasure both retain rows until the vacancy-close sweep. Every submission or erasure permanently burns a slot: ~500 lifetime applicants (organic on a high-traffic listing, or attacker aliases against the unauthenticated endpoint) wedge save-and-resume for the vacancy's entire life.
findings.recommended_fix: Add AND d.submitted_at IS NULL AND d.erased_at IS NULL to the cap count subquery so only live drafts consume the budget.

findings.title: Cap-blocked draft INSERT silently drops the save; handler answers ok:true and the client counts a phantom draft
findings.detail: At the cap the INSERT...SELECT yields zero rows; the upsert returns Ok(Returned(_, [])) and handle_save_draft maps any Ok(_) to {ok:true}. Combined with W3's attacker-fillable cap: a real applicant's saves vanish while the UI reports them safe and announceSaved fires a phantom application_draft_saved.
findings.recommended_fix: Distinguish zero-row causes (reason column via CTE, or pre-check cap for new pairs) and answer ok:false for the cap case; keep the silent-200 only for the deliberate submitted/erased guards.

findings.title: Fan-out 3/hour bound is check-then-act — concurrent cross-vacancy claims all pass
findings.detail: Concurrent claims for the same email on different vacancy rows update different rows (no lock interaction); each count subquery reads its statement-start snapshot under READ COMMITTED, so K simultaneous requests all see the pre-burst count and all send.
findings.recommended_fix: Serialise per-recipient (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(lower($2))) before the UPDATE) or accept-and-document the overshoot as an approximate bound.

findings.title: Fan-out bound and cooldown key on raw lower(email) — plus-addressed/dot aliases defeat the per-recipient protection while landing in one victim inbox
findings.detail: is_local_char allows '+' and '.'; drafts/claims key on the literal lowercased string. victim+1@gmail.com … victim+N@gmail.com are N distinct recipients to the bound (and N distinct 500-cap slots) but one inbox — the W6 fix's victim-spam protection is trivially bypassed for the dominant mailbox providers.
findings.recommended_fix: Canonicalise the recipient for cooldown/fan-out checks (strip +tag from the local part; strip dots for gmail.com/googlemail.com) so the bound applies per inbox, not per alias string.

findings.title: Resume start-step wiring branch (form-resume -> firstIncompleteIndex) pinned only at pure-function level
findings.detail: The frozen AC requires resume to start at the first incomplete section. firstIncompleteIndex has pure pins, but no test drives the stepper's initBrowser (grep confirms zero references in form_stepper.test.js) — reverting the marker ternary to 0 fails no test.
findings.recommended_fix: Drive the stepper init with a form-resume marker + fake sections and assert the starting index, mirroring form_draft_wiring.test.js's _initBrowser seam.

findings.title: claim_continue_link_send's submitted/erased zero-row guards unpinned (round-2 guard lines)
findings.detail: The claim matches by (vacancy,email), so only these two new lines stop a stripped or tombstoned row winning a claim, re-minting a token, and sending real email. Upsert and list guards are pinned; this query's are not.
findings.recommended_fix: Two integration cases: claim after strip_draft_on_submit and claim after erase_draft_by_token (same email) both return zero rows.

findings.title: form_draft.js loader inclusion unpinned on the pristine and error re-render pages
findings.detail: Deleting the script tag from the primary (or error) render silently kills the whole client-side save feature while every node-level wiring test stays green (they drive _initBrowser directly). Only the resume render has the pin (form_pages_test.gleam:334).
findings.recommended_fix: One-line assertions that view_application_page and view_form_with_errors output contain "/static/form_draft.js", mirroring the resume pin.

findings.title: Round-1 blocker fix (B1 origin-via-origin_domain) has zero automated pin — reverting to canonical_origin fails no test
findings.detail: The fix for the round-1 X-Forwarded-Host token-exfiltration blocker is new code with no regression pin: grep finds no build_entity_url test and no handler-level assertion of the emailed base. Given B1's severity (live-token exfiltration), the anti-regression pin matters.
findings.recommended_fix: Unit-test build_entity_url (domain selection + fallback), and pin the handler wiring by extracting the base-building decision as a pure function (origin_domain -> base) with tests, since Resend itself is not integration-testable.

findings.title: DOMContentLoaded bootstrap passes its Event into initBrowser's env parameter — latent (defer makes the 'loading' branch unreachable today)
findings.detail: addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initBrowser) would pass the Event as env; env.document is undefined so the !body guard returns and nothing wires. Unreachable while every renderer loads the script with defer (verified view_draft_saver_script emits defer), but one markup change away from silently disabling the saver. Demoted from blind's warning on verification.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap the listener: addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { initBrowser(); }).

findings.title: Migration header still claims lazy token minting and row-removal erasure — both reversed by the round-2 fixes in the same commit
findings.detail: 'most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on the first email-me-a-link request)' is false after W1 mint-at-save; 'erasure ... removes the row' contradicts the erased_at tombstone comment added below it. The schema file's own header misstates the GDPR model. (Migrations are immutable once merged — fix before merge.)
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the two header bullets to mint-at-save and tombstone semantics.

findings.title: Spec Suggested Review Order still describes the expiry sweep as 'closed, archived, or past closes_at' after W4 removed archived vacancies
findings.detail: The same file's round-2 changelog records W4; the navigation line was left describing the superseded sweep.
findings.recommended_fix: Edit to 'closed or past closes_at (archived vacancies keep drafts per W4)'.

findings.title: Vacancy closing mid-session disables the saver but leaves the save-and-continue promise and a deterministically-failing continue button
findings.detail: The closed arm sets saverDisabled but reconciles no UI: the swapped prep note keeps promising 'your answers save as you go', and a continue click maps the closed 200 {ok:false, closed:true} to 'Couldn't send the link just now — try again in a moment' though every retry deterministically fails.
findings.recommended_fix: On body.closed: restore the honest one-visit prep note and disable/relabel the continue button (or swap its copy to the closed message).

findings.title: Client-plausible but server-invalid email: saves 400 silently forever; continue-link misreports a deterministic rejection as transient
findings.detail: The client regex accepts addresses shared/email.is_valid rejects (1-char or numeric TLD, consecutive dots, hyphen-edged labels, non-ASCII). Every save gets a silent 400 (state stays dirty, never acknowledged) and the continue click shows 'try again in a moment' for a rejection that never clears.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the client predicate with the server rule (port is_valid's checks), or surface the 400 body distinctly in the continue-link status copy.

findings.title: 500-per-vacancy draft cap races concurrent inserts of distinct pairs (approximate bound)
findings.detail: The count<500 guard reads the inserting statement's snapshot; K concurrent saves for distinct new pairs all pass and all insert. Soft abuse bound — overshoot only, no corruption.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept and document the overshoot, or enforce atomically (vacancy-scoped advisory lock).

findings.title: resumed_at stamped for an empty-fields continue-link payload but not for the identical save payload
findings.detail: handle_save_draft's empty-filtered branch returns before the resume_token stamp; handle_continue_link stamps it for the same payload despite the 'Same re-engagement stamp' comment. The drafts-resumed funnel diverges by endpoint for identical client state.
findings.recommended_fix: Hoist (or skip) the stamp identically in both handlers when the payload carried no usable fields.

findings.title: Dead COALESCEs: claim RETURNING and list_resumable SELECT cannot observe a NULL continue_token
findings.detail: The SET clause guarantees non-NULL on returned rows and the IS NOT NULL filter makes the SELECT COALESCE dead; the inbound handler's token != '' guard then defends an impossible empty string.
findings.recommended_fix: Return/select continue_token bare and drop the empty-string guard, or keep one defensive COALESCE with a comment naming the legacy NULL case.

findings.title: DuplicateApplication branch never strips a coexisting live draft
findings.detail: A live draft can coexist with an application (no-JS/failed-save submit leaves no draft row; a later visit INSERTs a fresh draft — the upsert has no application-existence check). The duplicate branch renders the page without stripping: draft PII lingers and continue emails remain claimable for an applicant who already has an application.
findings.recommended_fix: Run the same fail-open strip_draft_on_submit on the DuplicateApplication branch, or add an application-existence guard to the upsert INSERT path.

findings.title: Draft upload-slot filter re-encodes document_upload's canonical slot-name whitelist
findings.detail: document_upload owns the names (private is_known_field plus pub *_key() fns whose docs forbid re-encoding); draft_handler hardcodes a second copy. The lists match today (verified: 5 primary + 2 co-applicant prefixes = full taxonomy) but a renamed/added slot silently escapes the draft filter.
findings.recommended_fix: Export a pub is_document_field/1 from document_upload and call it from is_file_slot_key; delete the re-encoded copy.

findings.title: Vacancy+draft lookup preamble triplicated across the three SSR draft handlers
findings.detail: handle_resume / handle_erasure_confirm / handle_erasure_delete repeat the same vacancy-lookup + friendly-404 + lookup_draft nesting (a distinct site from round-1 N6/N7).
findings.recommended_fix: Extract one with_vacancy_and_draft helper returning the shared 404/500 responses.

findings.title: Five draft copy constants in form_copy.gleam are unreferenced orphans — the KEEP-IN-SYNC mechanism has no mechanical guard
findings.detail: draft_prep_note, draft_continue_button, draft_continue_sent, draft_continue_needs_email, draft_continue_failed are read by no Gleam module or test (only a comment at form_view.gleam:124); the live strings live in form_draft.js and its test pins only the JS consts.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the five orphans, or pin form_draft.js strings against form_copy.gleam in a test.

findings.title: W9 closed-vacancy resume test asserts only absence of resume markers — an empty or 404 200-body passes
findings.detail: The test name claims the closed page renders, but nothing asserts closed-page content; view_closed_vacancy_page ships a unique data-testid="closed-vacancy-notice" (form_pages.gleam:31) that is left unasserted.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the body contains closed-vacancy-notice.

findings.title: W3 tombstone retains the erased applicant's plaintext email as suppression key (deliberate, documented — worth a conscious sign-off)
findings.detail: The round-2 erasure keeps the readable email until vacancy close as a suppression record (GDPR-recognised, disclosed on the confirm page, per the migration comment). A keyed hash satisfies the same re-save guard without retaining plaintext PII — flagged so the trade-off is explicit, not because the design is unexplained.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm the plaintext-suppression choice in the PR rationale (or switch the key to a keyed hash).

findings.title: Transfer-Encoding body-size rejection still tested POST-only after the N20 fix
findings.detail: Round-2 added PUT arms for over-limit and missing Content-Length but not for chunked TE; evaluate_body_size takes the method as an argument, so a method-conditioned TE arm would slip untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the TE rejection with http.Put.

findings.title: Erasure GET confirm on a never-valid token unpinned; only replay-after-tombstone POST 404 covered
findings.detail: The resume flow pins its uniform-404 (resume_with_unknown_token_is_uniform_404_test); the erasure GET confirm on a forged token — what a bad erasure link hits — has no test.
findings.recommended_fix: GET /apply/:code/draft-erasure/<forged> asserts the friendly 404 body.

findings.title: seed_draft_with_token mints 'tok-seed' via the upsert then overwrites with a redundant UPDATE
findings.detail: The round-2 upsert mints the token on INSERT, so passing the desired token as arg 4 reaches the same end state in one statement (upsert_mints_the_token_at_save_time_test proves it).
findings.recommended_fix: Pass `token` to the upsert and delete the UPDATE.

findings.title: list_resumable_draft_tokens lacks the erased_at guard every other W3-touched query has
findings.detail: Upsert and claim both guard erased_at IS NULL; the stage-2 prefetch does not — safe today only because erase_draft_by_token NULLs continue_token in the same UPDATE. A future path setting erased_at without NULLing the token would email an erased applicant.
findings.recommended_fix: Add AND erased_at IS NULL for symmetry (belt-and-braces).

findings.title: New token endpoints /apply/:code/resume/ and /apply/:code/draft-erasure/ lack the Cloudflare per-IP rule their same-model siblings (/erase/, /dsar/) got
findings.detail: The single http_ratelimit rule covers only /erase/ and /dsar/; the Worker limits only /api/v1/. The F3 capability endpoints share the identical anonymous 288-bit-token model (resume reads applicant PII, draft-erasure destroys it) but have no per-IP edge bound — the terraform comment's own brute-force/prefetch rationale applies equally.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the rule's expression to the two new path prefixes (or a follow-up ticket referencing this one).

findings.title: Four new public draft routes have no router-level pin; the /erase sibling has exactly that test
findings.detail: gdpr_integration_test drives POST /erase/:token through router.handle_request (lines 2069, 2130); every chunk-3 draft test calls handlers directly, so a route-table regression (verb mapping, path shape, SPA catch-all shadowing) fails no test.
findings.recommended_fix: One router.handle_request smoke test per draft route.

findings.title: vacancy_short_code helper duplicates gdpr_integration_test's fetch_vacancy_short_code (same directory, same query)
findings.detail: Third copy of the short_code-by-id lookup in the same test directory (application_integration_test.gleam:1727 inlines it too). AGENTS.md DRY rule: extract into integration/helpers.gleam.
findings.recommended_fix: Move one copy to helpers.gleam and reuse.

findings.title: Round-2 W7 test adds one-line alias wrappers form_view_now_ms / near_future_date instead of calling the real functions directly
findings.detail: Pure pass-through aliases used once each; the same directory calls the wrapped functions directly (application_integration_test.gleam:1812, 1820).

findings.title: Fan-out bound's 1-hour window value unpinned — only the count (3) is tested
findings.detail: A typo'd interval ('1 day') would pass the fan-out test identically; round 2 pinned the analogous 10-minute cooldown value (cooldown_window_is_ten_minutes_test) but not this window.
findings.recommended_fix: Backdate one stamped row by 61 minutes and assert it stops counting.

findings.title: Empty-fields no-wipe guard pinned on the save path only — handle_continue_link's [] -> skip-upsert branch untested
findings.detail: Round-1's guard applies to both handlers; only the save half has a regression pin. Testable without a real send by pre-stamping the cooldown, as the existing cooldown test does.
findings.recommended_fix: Continue-link call with empty fields on a cooldown-stamped draft asserts fields survive.

findings.title: Failed-save dirty-retry path in form_draft.js saveNow has no wiring test
findings.detail: The stated retry contract (non-OK response or rejected fetch leaves state dirty so the next trigger/beacon re-sends) is unpinned: form_draft_wiring.test.js covers success dedupe and the closed-vacancy terminal, never a transient failure followed by re-trigger.
findings.recommended_fix: One wiring test: first fetch rejects (or !ok), second trigger re-sends the same payload.

findings.title: application_draft updated_at trigger (N5 fix) has no test asserting it fires
findings.detail: The trigger is now the only updated_at writer on upsert/claim/mark_resumed; strip still SETs it manually, masking trigger loss on that path. No test references application_draft.updated_at.
findings.recommended_fix: Integration test: upsert, sleep-free second upsert (or claim), assert updated_at advanced.

rejected_findings.title: File-slot filter defines 5 primary document slots but only 2 co-applicant prefixes
